page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a high-capacity virtual server featuring 144 vCPUs and 540 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, this server allocates 72 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a substantial 504 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-144 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU scores. Its memory architecture delivers exceptional throughput, with cached read bandwidth reaching 11,548.62 GB/sec and uncached large-block write bandwidth at 213.92 GB/sec. The hardware excels in cryptographic operations, database transactions, and static web serving, while also showing strong capabilities in LLM prompt processing and multi-threaded decompression. However, single-core CPU performance is more moderate, placing in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density and compute power per virtual machine instance, making it highly suitable for consolidating massive enterprise workloads without the overhead of multiple smaller nodes. Lacking local storage and integrated GPUs, it relies on network-attached storage and is optimized strictly for CPU-bound tasks. This profile makes the c4-standard-144 highly suited for high-performance computing (HPC), large-scale database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
